title.zh: 卷十五 志第七 州郡下
title.raw: 卷十五 志第七 州郡下 Volume 15 Treatises 7: Administrative Districts 2

sentences.zh: 荊 巴 郢 司 雍 湘 梁 秦 益 寧

translations.literal: Jing, Ba, Ying, Si, Yong, Xiang, Liang, Qin, Yi, Ning
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Ba, Ying, Si, Yong, Xiang, Liang, Qin, Yi, Ning

sentences.zh: 漢靈帝中平末刺史王睿始治江陵，吳時西陵督鎮之。

translations.literal: At the end of Han Emperor Ling's Zhongping era, Inspector Wang Rui first governed from Jiangling; in Wu times the Xiling garrison commandant was stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Han Lingdi's Zhongping reign, Inspector Wang Rui first took Jiangling as his seat; under Wu, the Xiling garrison commandant held it.

sentences.zh: 晉太康元年平吳，以爲刺史治。

translations.literal: In Jin Taikang year 1 Wu was pacified, and it was made the inspector's seat.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taikang 1, after the conquest of Wu, it became the provincial seat.

sentences.zh: 愍帝建興元年，刺史周顗避杜弢賊奔建康，陶侃爲刺史，治沌口。

translations.literal: In Emperor Min's Jianxing year 1, Inspector Zhou Yi fled the bandit Du Tao to Jiankang; Tao Kan became inspector and governed from Zhunkou.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Min's Jianxing 1, Inspector Zhou Yi fled Du Tao's rebels to Jiankang; Tao Kan succeeded as inspector and sat at Zhunkou.

sentences.zh: 其後或還江陵，或在夏口。

translations.literal: Afterward they sometimes returned to Jiangling, sometimes sat at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the seat shifted between Jiangling and Xiakou.

translations.literal: Huan Wen pacified Shu and governed from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen pacified Shu and returned the seat to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 以臨沮西界，水陸紆險，行逕裁通，南通巴、巫，東南出州治，道帶蠻、蜑，田土肥美，立爲汶陽郡，以處流民。

translations.literal: Because the western border of Linju was winding and perilous by water and land, routes barely passable, south connecting Ba and Wu and southeast leading out from the provincial seat—the road runs through Man and Dan peoples, the fields fertile and fine—Wenyang Commandery was established to settle refugees.
translations.idiomatic: West of Linju the land and water routes were tortuous and dangerous, passable only with difficulty; south lay Ba and Wu, southeast the road out to the provincial seat ran through Man and Dan country, and the soil was rich—so Wenyang commandery was set up for displaced people.

sentences.zh: 屬氐陷襄陽，桓沖避居上明，頓陸遜樂鄉城上四十餘里，以田地肥良，可以爲軍民資實，又接近三峽，無西疆之虞，故重戍江南，輕戍江北。

translations.literal: When the Di seized Xiangyang, Huan Chong moved to Shangming and encamped above Lu Xun's Lecheng fortress by forty-odd li—the farmland was rich and could supply military and civilian stores, and it was close to the Three Gorges with no worry on the western frontier, so they heavily garrisoned the south of the Jiang and lightly garrisoned the north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di took Xiangyang, Huan Chong withdrew to Shangming and camped forty-odd li above Lu Xun's fortress at Lecheng; the fields were fertile enough to feed army and people, and the site lay near the Three Gorges with no threat from the west—so garrisons were weighted on the south bank and thinned on the north.

translations.literal: After Fu Jian's defeat, they regained Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Jian's defeat, Xiangyang was recovered.

sentences.zh: 太元十四年，王忱還江陵。

translations.literal: In Taixuan year 14, Wang Chen returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixuan 14, Wang Chen returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江陵去襄陽步道五百，勢同脣齒，無襄陽則江陵受敵，不立故也。

translations.literal: Jiangling to Xiangyang by foot route is five hundred li; the positions are like lips and teeth—without Xiangyang, Jiangling takes the enemy, which is why it was not left undefended.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling lies five hundred li from Xiangyang on foot; the two stand like lips and teeth—without Xiangyang, Jiangling is exposed to attack, and for that reason the link was never abandoned.

translations.literal: Since Chen, it has not been moved again.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chen's time the seat has not moved again.

sentences.zh: 境域之內，含帶蠻、蜑，土地遼落，稱爲殷曠。

translations.literal: Within the borders it embraces Man and Dan peoples; the land is vast and spread out, called abundant and open.
translations.idiomatic: Inside its borders live Man and Dan peoples; the territory is broad and thinly settled, yet reckoned rich and spacious.

translations.literal: Among the great garrisons of Jiangzuo, none surpass Jing and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Of the great strongholds south of the Yangtze, none match Jing and Yang.

sentences.zh: 弘農郡陝縣，周世二伯總諸侯，周公主陝東，召公主陝西，故稱荊州爲陝西也。

translations.literal: In Hongnong Commandery, Shan County—in Zhou times the Two Lords assembled the feudal lords; the Duke of Zhou held east of Shan, the Duke of Shao west of Shan—hence Jing Province is called Shan-west.
translations.idiomatic: Shan county in Hongnong commandery: in Zhou times the Two Lords mustered the feudal lords; the Duke of Zhou held the east of Shan, the Duke of Shao the west—hence Jing province is called Shan-west.

宋景平初，失河南地，元嘉末，僑立州於汝南縣瓠，尋罷。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song Jingping, Henan territory was lost; at the end of Yuanjia a refugee province was established at Hu in Runan county and soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Song Jingping, Henan was lost; late in Yuanjia a refugee province was set up at Hu in Runan county, then soon abolished.

translations.literal: The province was established at Yiyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The province was established at Yiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 有三關之隘，北接陳、汝，控帶許、洛。

translations.literal: It had the narrow passes of the Three Gates, bordered Chen and Ru to the north, and controlled Xu and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: It held the Three Gates narrows, linked north to Chen and Ru, and controlled the Xu region and Luoyang.

translations.literal: From then on it was constantly a border garrison.
translations.idiomatic: From then on it served constantly as a border fortress.

sentences.zh: 泰始旣遷，領義陽，僑立汝南，領三郡。

translations.literal: Once Taishi had passed and it was moved, it governed Yiyang, established refugee Runan, and administered three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taishi move it held Yiyang, set up refugee Runan, and governed three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，又領安陸、隨、安蠻三郡。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui year 4 it also administered Anlu, Sui, and Anman—three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui 4 it also took Anlu, Sui, and Anman—three commanderies.

鎮襄陽，晉中朝荊州都督所治也。

translations.literal: Garrisoned at Xiangyang—it was the seat of the Jin central-court Inspector-General of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The seat lay at Xiangyang; in the Jin central court it was where the Inspector-General of Jing sat.

sentences.zh: 元帝以魏該爲雍州，鎮酇城，襄陽別有重戍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan made Wei Gai Inspector of Yong and garrisoned Zuo city; Xiangyang separately had a heavy garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan made Wei Gai inspector of Yong and sat at Zuo city; Xiangyang kept a separate strong garrison.

sentences.zh: 庾翼爲荊州，謀北伐，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Yu Yi was Inspector of Jing, planned a northern expedition, and garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi held Jing province, planned a northern campaign, and garrisoned Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉亂，襄陽民戶流荒。

translations.literal: Since the Yongjia turmoil, Xiangyang's registered households were scattered and wasted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia upheaval, Xiangyang's registered households were driven off and the land lay empty.

sentences.zh: 咸康八年，尚書殷融言：「襄陽、石城，疆埸之地，對接荒寇。

translations.literal: In Xiankang year 8, Minister of the Masters of Writing Yin Rong said: 「Xiangyang and Shicheng are frontier ground, facing wild raiders.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang 8, Minister of the Masters of Writing Yin Rong said: 「Xiangyang and Shicheng are border posts hard against barbarian enemies.

sentences.zh: 諸荒殘寄治郡縣，民戶寡少，可幷合之。

translations.literal: The various wasted remnants lodged in commanderies and counties have few households; they may be merged.」
translations.idiomatic: Refugee districts set up for the ruined borderlands have too few households; they should be consolidated.」

sentences.zh: 」朱序爲雍州，於襄陽立僑郡縣，沒苻氐。

translations.literal: Zhu Xu was Inspector of Yong; at Xiangyang he established refugee commanderies and counties, and was lost to Fu Jian's Di.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xu became inspector of Yong, set up refugee commanderies and counties at Xiangyang, and the region fell to Fu Jian's Di.

translations.literal: When the Di were defeated, he returned south again, and Zhu Xu was again employed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Di were beaten, the seat returned south, and Zhu Xu was again put in charge.

sentences.zh: 襄陽左右，田土肥良，桑梓野澤，處處而有。

translations.literal: Around Xiangyang the fields are fertile and fine; mulberry groves and wild marshes are everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: On either side of Xiangyang the soil is rich; mulberry hamlets and marshland appear at every turn.

sentences.zh: 郗恢爲雍州，于時舊民甚少，新戶稍多。

translations.literal: Xi Hui was Inspector of Yong; at the time the old residents were very few, and new households somewhat more.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Hui held Yong; by then the long-settled people were few, while newer registrations were somewhat greater.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉中，割荊州五郡屬，遂爲大鎮。

translations.literal: In Song Yuanjia, five Jing commanderies were cut off and attached, and it thus became a great garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia five Jing commanderies were detached and placed under it, and it became a major stronghold.

sentences.zh: 疆蠻帶沔，阻以重山，北接宛、洛，平塗直至，跨對樊、沔，爲鄢郢北門。

translations.literal: Its border touches the Man; it belts the Mian; heavy mountains block it; north it meets Wan and Luo by level road direct; spanning and facing Fan and Mian, it is the north gate of Yan and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier runs with the Man; the Han River threads through it; great mountains bar the way; northward Wan and Luo lie on a straight level road; facing Fan and the Han across the water, it is the northern gate of Yan and Ying.

sentences.zh: 部領蠻左，故別置蠻府焉。

translations.literal: It administers the Many on the left, so a separate Man office was established.
translations.idiomatic: It oversees the left-side Man peoples, and for that reason a separate Man headquarters was set up.

translations.literal: It was established in Jin Emperor Wu's Taishi year 5.

sentences.zh: 舊土有秦之富，跨帶壠坂。

translations.literal: The old territory had Qin's wealth, spanning hills and ridges.
translations.idiomatic: The original land held Qin's riches, belted with loess hills and ridges.

sentences.zh: 太康省，惠帝元康七年復置。

translations.literal: Abolished in Taikang; restored in Emperor Hui's Yuankang 7.
translations.idiomatic: Abolished in Taikang; restored in Emperor Hui's Yuankang 7.

translations.literal: When the Central Plains fell into turmoil, it was lost to the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Central Plains fell into chaos, it was lost to the northerners.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和八年，胡偽秦州刺史王擢降，仍以爲刺史，尋爲苻健所破。

translations.literal: In Emperor Mu's Yonghe 8, Wang Zhuo, the Hu puppet inspector of Qin, surrendered and was kept as inspector; soon Fu Jian defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Mu's Yonghe 8, Wang Zhuo, the Later Zhao puppet inspector of Qin, surrendered and was kept in post; soon Fu Jian defeated him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，桓溫以氐王楊國爲秦州刺史，未有民土。

translations.literal: In year 11, Huan Wen made the Di king Yang Guo inspector of Qin; there was no settled populace or territory.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, Huan Wen made the Di king Yang Guo inspector of Qin, but he held no settled land or people.

sentences.zh: 至泰元十四年，雍州刺史朱序始督秦州，則孝武所置也。

translations.literal: By Taixuan 14, Yongzhou Inspector Zhu Xu first oversaw Qin—this was Emperor Xiaowu's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: By Taixuan 14, Yongzhou inspector Zhu Xu first oversaw Qin—an arrangement of Emperor Xiaowu's reign.

sentences.zh: 寄治襄陽，未有刺史，是後雍州刺史常督之。

translations.literal: The seat was lodged at Xiangyang; there was no [separate] inspector; thereafter the Yongzhou inspector regularly oversaw it.
translations.idiomatic: The seat lodged at Xiangyang with no separate inspector; thereafter the Yongzhou inspector regularly oversaw it.

sentences.zh: 隆安二年，郭銓始爲梁、南秦州刺史，州寄治漢中。

translations.literal: In Long'an 2, Guo Quan first became inspector of Liang and Southern Qin; the province seat was lodged at Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Long'an 2, Guo Quan first became inspector of Liang and Southern Qin, with the provincial seat lodged at Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 四年，桓玄督七州，但云秦州。

translations.literal: In year 4, Huan Xuan oversaw seven provinces, naming only Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Huan Xuan oversaw seven provinces but named only Qin.

sentences.zh: 元興元年，以苻堅子宏爲北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yuanxing 1, Fu Jian's son Hong was made inspector of North Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxing 1, Fu Jian's son Hong was made inspector of North Qin.

sentences.zh: 自此荊州都督常督秦州，梁州常帶南秦州刺史。

translations.literal: From this time the Jingzhou overseer regularly oversaw Qin; Liang province regularly carried the Southern Qin inspector's title.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the Jingzhou overseer regularly oversaw Qin, while the Liang inspector regularly held the title of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 義熙三年，以氐王楊國爲北秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yixi 3, the Di king Yang Guo was made inspector of North Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi 3, the Di king Yang Guo was made inspector of North Qin.

sentences.zh: 十四年，置東秦州，劉義真爲刺史。

translations.literal: In year 14, East Qin was established; Liu Yizhen became inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, East Qin was established and Liu Yizhen made inspector.

sentences.zh: 郭恭爲梁州刺史，尹雅爲秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Guo Gong was inspector of Liang; Yin Ya was inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Gong was inspector of Liang; Yin Ya was inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝爲荊州都督，督秦州，又進督北秦州。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Song as Jingzhou overseer oversaw Qin and further advanced to oversee North Qin.
translations.idiomatic: As Jingzhou overseer, Emperor Wen of Song oversaw Qin and later also oversaw North Qin.

translations.literal: Provincial names appeared mixed; abolitions and establishments are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial names appear inconsistently; which posts were abolished or restored is unclear.

sentences.zh: 《永明郡國志》秦州寄治漢中南鄭，不曰南北。

translations.literal: The Gazetteer of Commanderies and Principalities of Yongming places Qin's seat lodged at Nanzheng in Hanzhong, without north-south distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongming Gazetteer of Commanderies and Principalities places Qin lodged at Nanzheng in Hanzhong, with no north-south distinction.

sentences.zh: 《元嘉計偕》亦云秦州，而荊州都督常督二秦，梁、南秦一刺史。

translations.literal: The Yuanjia Tribute Register also names only Qin, while the Jingzhou overseer regularly oversaw the two Qins and Liang and Southern Qin had one inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanjia Tribute Register likewise names only Qin, yet the Jingzhou overseer regularly oversaw both Qins, and Liang and Southern Qin shared one inspector.

sentences.zh: 是則《志》所載秦州爲南秦，氐爲北秦。

translations.literal: Thus the Qin recorded in the Gazetteer is Southern Qin; the Di held North Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Qin in the Gazetteer is Southern Qin; the Di held North Qin.

sentences.zh: 開拓夷荒，稍成郡縣，如漢之永昌，晉之雲山之類是也。

translations.literal: Opening up barbarian wilds, it gradually became commanderies and counties, like Han's Yongchang or Jin's Yunshan.
translations.idiomatic: By opening the frontier to barbarian lands it gradually gained commanderies and counties, as with Han's Yongchang or Jin's Yunshan.

sentences.zh: 蜀侯惲壯以來，四爲偏據，故諸葛亮云「益州險塞，沃野天府」。

translations.literal: Since Marquis Yun of Shu came of age, four times it has been held in separate rule; hence Zhuge Liang said, "Yi Province is strategically sealed, with fertile fields like Heaven's storehouse."
translations.idiomatic: Since the Marquis of Shu reached his prime, the region has four times been held apart; hence Zhuge Liang's line that Yi Province is strategically sealed, with fertile fields like Heaven's storehouse.

sentences.zh: 劉頌亦謂「成都宜處親子弟，以爲王國」。

translations.literal: Liu Song also said, "Chengdu is fit to place a kinsman's son, making it a princely state."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Song likewise held that Chengdu should lodge a prince of the imperial line as a royal domain.

sentences.zh: 故立成都王穎，竟不之國。

translations.literal: Therefore Prince of Chengdu Ying was established, but in the end he never went to his state.
translations.idiomatic: A Prince of Chengdu, Ying, was therefore enfeoffed, but he never took up residence there.

translations.literal: The Three Gorges are perilous and blocked; barbarians are exceedingly fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Gorges are perilous; barbarian power runs very strong.

sentences.zh: 西通芮芮河南，亦如漢武威張掖，爲西域之道也。

translations.literal: West it connects with Rouran south of the Yellow River, also like Han's Wuwei and Zhangye—as a route to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: To the west it reaches Rouran territory south of the Yellow River, and like Han Wuwei and Zhangye it forms the road into the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 方面疆鎮，塗出萬里，晉世以處武臣。

translations.literal: A frontier garrison province; roads extend ten thousand li—the Jin era posted martial officials there.
translations.idiomatic: A border garrison province with routes stretching ten thousand li; under Jin it was held by military men.

sentences.zh: 宋世亦以險遠，諸王不牧。

translations.literal: In the Song era too, because of peril and distance, princes did not govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song as well, its danger and remoteness kept princes from taking it as a fief.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，成都市橋忽生小洲，始康人邵碩有術數，見之曰：「洲生近市，當有貴王臨境。

translations.literal: In Taishi, a small islet suddenly grew at Chengdu's market bridge. Shao Shuo of Shikang, skilled in numerology, seeing it said: "An islet born near the market—there will be an honored prince at the border.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era a small islet suddenly rose beside Chengdu's market bridge. Shao Shuo of Shikang, versed in divination, said on seeing it, "An islet beside the market means a noble prince will come to the border.

sentences.zh: 」永明二年，而始興王鎮爲刺史。

translations.literal: when split they might exceed thirteen; combined they did not pass nine.
translations.idiomatic: split, they might run past thirteen; merged, they rarely held at nine.

translations.literal: Cities and settlements were parcelled out; titles and names grew thick.
translations.idiomatic: Towns and fiefs were carved out, names and ranks piled high.

translations.literal: Migrations and rebellions—one generation passed, another arose.
translations.idiomatic: Through flight and revolt, one age died and another was born.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text has used as the base for collation the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi, January 1972.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi (January 1972).
